provenance.instrument: Code of the Township of Radnor, Chapter 280 Zoning, as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 (code RA0484): includes legislation through 09-28-2026. New Laws lists two ordinances, for Chapter 250 and Chapter 270. Neither touches zoning. The chapter was read in the eCode360 print view in a browser.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360: Includes legislation through 09-28-2026. New Laws (2), none for Chapter 280.
checks: The zoning code has no accessory dwelling unit or accessory apartment rule for house lots. R-1 to R-4 list single-family detached dwellings, a few special exceptions and listed accessory uses (280-14, 280-17.2, 280-19, 280-24, 280-29)
A dwelling unit may have 'not more than one kitchen' and a family is one housekeeping unit (280-4). A second kitchen unit is a second dwelling unit

Uses the code does not define go to R-6 or PA only, by conditional use (280-130.1). A second unit is not such a use: conversions to two-family use and two-family dwellings are defined and listed (280-108, 280-34C). In R-1 to R-4 the path is a use variance

AC district only: a tenant house is a listed accessory use on a lot of at least four acres, for tenant farmers or employees of a farm or estate (280-9H(3), 280-4). It is not an ADU. It is recorded as an alternative

Conversion of a house to two units is a special exception in AC, R-1 and R-2 (280-108), and in R-3 by reference to 280-14B (280-24B(1)). R-1A and R-4 adopt only the uses 'permitted' in R-1 and R-3, so the conversion likely does not reach them (medium confidence, ask the township). Each unit needs the district single-family lot area (75% of it for dwellings of 10,000 sq ft or more) and at least 600 sq ft. No exterior extension
Two-family detached dwellings are permitted in R-5. Lot area 5,445 sq ft per family, 80 ft wide (280-34C, 280-35A(1))
Parking: two spaces per dwelling unit (280-103B(1))
Rental units need an annual license from the township, with inspections (226-7)
Accessory buildings: 20 ft high, 10 ft from the house. Side and rear 10 ft in R-1 to R-3, 3 ft in R-4, 20 ft in AC (280-12, 280-17, 280-22, 280-27, 280-32)
Garrett Hill GH-GA lists a 'Commercial structure containing one accessory dwelling unit' as a mixed use (280-49.7). That is a unit in a commercial building, not a backyard unit

Nonconforming lots: a lot of record in single and separate ownership since before March 9, 1928 may get a single-family detached dwelling if it has at least 80% of the district minimum lot area. Nothing in 280-176 allows a second unit (280-176A, C)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Community Development Department, https://www.radnor.com/government/departments/community-development. Searched Chapter 280 for: accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, in-law, granny, elder, ECHO, carriage, guest, servant, caretaker, secondary dwelling, accessory living, second dwelling, accessory residential, living quarters, kitchen, tenant house. Review fixes 2026-11-11: tenant house moved to alternatives, R-6 and PA conditional-use path removed. Pending: no zoning amendment on the New Laws list.

term.note: No ADU term. Searched for accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, in-law, granny, elder, ECHO, carriage, servant, caretaker, second dwelling. The AC 'tenant house' is housing for 'tenant farmers or employees of a farm or estate' (280-4). It is recorded as an alternative.

status.note: The code has no ADU text for house lots.

path.note: R-1 to R-4 list no second unit. 280-130.1 reaches only uses 'not specifically defined', and two-family use and conversions are defined. A use variance is the path. Where it reaches, the 280-108 conversion is a special exception (alternatives).

value.name: Tenant house (accessory building, AC only)
value.conditions: Only for 'tenant farmers or employees of a farm or estate' (280-4). Lot of at least four acres. Lot restricted against further subdivision unless the tenant house could meet Chapter 255. AC accessory buildings: 20 ft high, 20 ft from side and rear lines, 10 ft from the house.

value.name: Conversion of a house to two units
value.conditions: Existing dwelling. Lot area per unit at least the district single-family lot area (2 acres). Each unit 600 sq ft or more, separate access, no exterior extension except for safety. Dwellings of 10,000 sq ft or more need 75% of that lot area per unit.

value.name: Conversion of a house to two units
value.conditions: Existing dwelling. Lot area per unit at least 1 acre. Each unit 600 sq ft or more, separate access, no exterior extension except for safety. 75% of the lot area per unit for dwellings of 10,000 sq ft or more.

value.name: Conversion of a house to two units
value.conditions: Existing dwelling. Lot area per unit at least 20,000 sq ft. Each unit 600 sq ft or more, separate access, no exterior extension except for safety. Dwellings of 10,000 sq ft or more need 75% of that lot area per unit.

value.name: Conversion of a house to two units
value.conditions: Listed in R-3 by reference to 280-14B (280-24B(1)). 280-108 itself names AC, R-1 and R-2. Lot area per unit at least 10,000 sq ft, 75% of it for dwellings of 10,000 sq ft or more. Each unit 600 sq ft or more, separate access, no exterior extension.

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling
value.conditions: Lot area 5,445 sq ft per family and 80 ft lot width. Side yards 10 ft each.

alternatives.note: Two-unit lot figures are twice the per-unit lot area. The conversion likely does not reach R-1A or R-4: 280-17.2A and 280-29A adopt only uses 'permitted' in R-1 and R-3 (medium confidence).

value.condition: AC accessory structures: 20 ft from a side or rear property line and 10 ft from the house. 20 ft high.
R-4 accessory structures: 3 ft from a side or rear property line (10 ft in R-1 to R-3).
A rented unit needs an annual rental license from the township, with inspections.
